Targets multi-column reading-order/label salience errors. Right column (Bill To) is large and prominent; left column (Vendor of record) is smaller. Vision models often pick the salient right-side entity as the vendor. Text-only verifier can resolve via explicit label. Not covered by existing traps; expect Gemini Flash to confuse roles more often than Claude/GPT.

A decoy value is visually redacted with a black vector box and 'REDACTED' text, but remains in the PDF's text stream. The correct value appears elsewhere. This tests if a model can interpret the visual semantics of redaction, or if it naively trusts the underlying text stream. Targets a gap between vector-text codepoint awareness and pixel-only reading. Two identical-looking 'TOTAL' rows differ only by ASCII O vs Cyrillic U+041E; a printed clause says which codepoint is binding. Models that read raw text (or strong reasoners) resolve it; vision-only or weaker models can't tell the labels apart and guess. Distinct from existing footnote/redaction/multi-column traps — this probes Unicode-awareness in document grounding. Expect Gemini Flash and GPT-4o to fail; Sonnet/Opu

Targets visual-text integration: a large diagonal watermark with a conflicting amount competes with the clear FINAL amount. Vision models often overweight salience and pick the watermark, while careful readers follow the explicit policy line. Distinct from small-print/hidden-text traps; probes susceptibility to background overlays. Expect Gemini Flash to misread salience more than Claude/GPT.

Targets visual-vector reasoning: a thin strike-through line crosses out a decoy amount, with the correct amount written beside it. This pattern mimics manual corrections. Text extraction captures both numbers but loses the visual 'negation' cue of the line. A model that fails to ground the text in the visual vector information will likely return the more prominent (but incorrect) decoy amount. This is a pure visual semantics test not covered by existing traps.

Targets vision-model weakness on rotated text. Many VLM pipelines tokenize pages in canonical orientation; 90deg sideways text is often misread, skipped, or treated as decoration. Text-extraction pipelines read it fine (characters are in the stream). Humans tilt their head or the viewer. Distinct from existing traps (small-print, hidden-OCR, Unicode, footnote): this probes orientation-equivariance specifically. Targets cross-currency reasoning: the page headlines a EUR total while a clear settlement clause requires USD payment at a stated FX rate. Many VLMs grab the salient EUR figure or fail to apply conversion/rounding. Text-only extraction plus reasoning resolves it. Distinct from small-print/hidden-text: this probes arithmetic + policy compliance. Expect weaker models (e.g., Haiku, some Flash variants) to answer the EUR amount or $-prefixed EUR.

This creates a gap between pipelines that only extract the primary text stream vs. those that can interpret richer PDF semantics. Humans see the note immediately. Targets vision-pipeline orientation sensitivity. The binding amount is in 11pt text rotated 90deg along the right margin — fully legible to humans (head tilt) and trivial for text extractors (characters in the stream regardless of rotation), but many VLMs tokenize at canonical orientation and skip/under-attend to sideways text. Distinct from small-print, hidden-OCR, Unicode, footnote, currency traps. Expect Haiku/Flash-lite to miss; Opus/GPT-5/Gemini-Pro to handle rotation. Previous attempt fail
